chapter: Origins of jazz and the district
title: Never played in the district; Fisher and Blessing bands
summary: His band never played the district, the name jazz arrived in Chicago, Fisher's band was good, and Tom's success drew copycat bands.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did your band ever play any jobs at all in the district, in any of the dance halls any time?

No, not in any... No, no. Never in the district. As I told you before, our music, our type of music wouldn't be acceptable there. It wouldn't fit in with that type of... But yet the writers would try to have people believe that that type of music, jazz music, originated... It didn't. It was an entirely different music in the arts.
What did they play at Seventh and Magazine? We played...

We played what we call the right time at that time. See, it was the same type of music that Tom played at Seventh and Magazine. He played in Chicago. That was named jazz then after it got up there. But before that, the people in New Orleans as itself, we never knew anything about jazz. We never thought of calling it jazz. But after it got up there, they called it jazz.
Now, Mr. Cook, you mentioned some good bands at Seventh and Magazine. No, the only two I said that they had in the city was Blessing and Brown. Blessing.
Don't you remember Fisher's band? Fisher, yeah.

He had a good orchestra too. I don't remember so much... Who was Blessing? Blessing. That was Blessing's band, wasn't it? Blessing. Blessing. He played trumpet. And I don't know much about his band at all. We were speaking about our section. No. We'll have to look up on Blessing. I don't think you'll find anyone in his band living yet, huh?
No. Because I don't know. He's...

The only ones that I remember is that really were considered good was Fisher's band and my brother's band. And we did if... I'm not bragging, but we did have one of the best bands down here. And that's why when Tom went up there and was so successful, the people were all waiting a block or so to gain admittance. Other cafe owners, they were losing business so fast that they told the unionists, they said, well, you have to do something about that. He said, we... We're losing business. And the fellow says, well, the only thing I can tell you to do is to go down to New Orleans and try to get a band similar to the one that Browns got and try to compete. So they did. They come down and picked up any band that said that they had a band similar to Tom's band. And so everything centers around Tom in that particular area. Now, Gussie Mueller, he played with different orchestras and also Ray Lopez. And by the way, before you leave, I'll try to give you the address of...
